ungrounded.answer:
The solubility of Al(OH)_3 in pure water is approximately 5.8 × 10^-3 mol L^-1.

Work:
- Combined reaction Al(OH)_3(s) + OH^- ⇌ Al(OH)_4^- has K = K_sp·K_f = (5.3×10^-27)(1.1×10^31) = 5.83×10^4.
- In pure water [OH^-] = 1.0×10^-7 mol/L (from K_w = 1.0×10^-14).
- Complex term: [Al(OH)_4^-] = K·[OH^-] = (5.83×10^4)(1.0×10^-7) = 5.83×10^-3 mol/L.
- Free-ion term: [Al^3+] = K_sp/[OH^-]^3 = 5.3×10^-27/(1.0×10^-7)^3 = 5.3×10^-6 mol/L.
- Total S = [Al^3+] + [Al(OH)_4^-] = 5.3×10^-6 + 5.83×10^-3 = 5.835×10^-3 mol/L.

The hydroxo-complex Al(OH)_4^- dominates, so S ≈ 5.8 × 10^-3 mol L^-1.

grounded.answer:
S ≈ 1.8 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ (rigorous, charge-balance closure)

If instead the standard textbook approximation [OH⁻] = 1.0×10⁻⁷ is imposed (the value the problem likely intends), then S ≈ 5.8 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹. NOTE: [OH⁻]=10⁻⁷ is NOT self-consistent here, so 1.8×10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ is the defensible answer.</answer>
<parameter name="work">GIVEN (only these): K_sp[Al(OH)₃] = 5.3×10⁻²⁷ ; K_f[Al(OH)₄⁻] = 1.1×10³¹.
IMPORTED STANDARD CONSTANT (flagged, not in problem): K_w = 1.0×10⁻¹⁴ — needed for Equation C; any numeric answer is conditional on this import.

Species (Al³⁺, Al(OH)₄⁻ only; intermediate hydroxo-complexes neglected, K_f not given). Solubility S = [Al³⁺] + [Al(OH)₄⁻].

Combined constant: K_c = K_sp·K_f = (5.3×10⁻²⁷)(1.1×10³¹) = 5.83×10⁴, for Al(OH)₃(s) + OH⁻ ⇌ Al(OH)₄⁻, so [Al(OH)₄⁻] = K_c·[OH⁻].

GOVERNING SYSTEM (4 unknowns: [Al³⁺], [Al(OH)₄⁻], [H⁺], [OH⁻]):
  A (K_sp):    [Al³⁺][OH⁻]³ = 5.3×10⁻²⁷
  B (K_c):     [Al(OH)₄⁻] = 5.83×10⁴·[OH⁻]
  C (K_w, imported): [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0×10⁻¹⁴
  D (charge balance): 3[Al³⁺] + [H⁺] = [OH⁻] + [Al(OH)₄⁻]

Substituting A, B, C into D gives one equation in [OH⁻]:
  3(5.3×10⁻²⁷)/[OH⁻]³ + (1.0×10⁻¹⁴)/[OH⁻] = [OH⁻] + 5.83×10⁴·[OH⁻].

WHY THE [OH⁻]=10⁻⁷ PIN FAILS: the dominant pathway is the amphoteric dissolution Al(OH)₃ + OH⁻ → Al(OH)₄⁻, which CONSUMES net OH⁻, pulling the solution mildly acidic. Solving D does not return 10⁻⁷.

NUMERIC ROOT (verified by bisection; charge-balance residual ~2×10⁻¹⁹):
  [OH⁻] = 2.29×10⁻⁸ M  (pH = 6.36, [H⁺] = 4.38×10⁻⁷ M)
  [Al³⁺]    = K_sp/[OH⁻]³ = 4.44×10⁻⁴ M
  [Al(OH)₄⁻] = K_c·[OH⁻]  = 1.33×10⁻³ M
  S = [Al³⁺] + [Al(OH)₄⁻] = 1.78×10⁻³ ≈ 1.8×10⁻³ mol L⁻¹.

In this regime the H⁺ and free-OH⁻ terms (~10⁻⁷) are negligible against the ~10⁻³ Al terms, so D collapses to the clean dominant balance 3[Al³⁺] = [Al(OH)₄⁻], i.e. 3K_sp/[OH⁻]³ = K_c[OH⁻] → [OH⁻]⁴ = 3K_sp/K_c = 2.73×10⁻³¹ → [OH⁻] = 2.29×10⁻⁸ M, reproducing S = 1.78×10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ analytically.

CONTRAST — textbook approximation: forcing [OH⁻]=10⁻⁷ gives [Al(OH)₄⁻]=K_c·10⁻⁷=5.83×10⁻³ and [Al³⁺]=5.3×10⁻⁶, so S ≈ 5.8×10⁻³ mol L⁻¹. This is the value the problem most likely expects, but it rests on an unjustified, self-inconsistent [OH⁻] pin.

DELIVERABLE: coupled system {A, B, C, D}; flag that K_w = 1.0×10⁻¹⁴ is an imported standard constant absent from the problem; and that [OH⁻] must be solved (= 2.29×10⁻⁸ M), not fixed at 10⁻⁷.</work>
</invoke>
